newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian bank objects to Moody's rating.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian bank objects to Moody's rating.

text.p: Egyptian American Bank said on Wednesday it objected to the bank financial strength rating it was awarded by Moody's this week.

"We do not agree with the D+ financial strength rating and would appreciate you explanation as to why we did not have a C or C+ rating," EAB managing director Gary Johns said in a letter to Moody's, copied to Reuters.
"We also analyse our competitive banks in detail and see no reason for the lower rating you have given EAB," he added.
Moody's gave a C bank financial strength rating to Egypt's Commercial International Bank (CIB) and a D rating to Misr International Bank/MIBank.
All three banks received a Ba3/Not Prime long and short-term rating for deposits.
